comparisons.peer_topic: Components of Capital Requirements and G-SIB Surcharge
comparisons.peer_summary: Capital requirements include buffers such as the 2.5% advanced capital buffer, SCB, countercyclical buffer, and a G-SIB surcharge of 3.0% for 2024-2025, expected to rise to 3.5% in 2026; these may vary due to regulatory guidance, positional changes, or stress test results.
comparisons.comparison: Both BAC and GS disclose the specific components of their CET1 regulatory minimums and buffers. Both identify a G-SIB surcharge of 3.0% for 2024. However, they differ in the Capital Conservation Buffer (CCB) structure: BAC utilizes a Stress Capital Buffer (SCB) of 3.2% under the Standardized Approach, whereas GS identifies a fixed 2.5% advanced capital buffer and a variable SCB under its capital requirements framework.

sentences.text: (2)The CET1 capital regulatory minimum is the sum of the CET1 capital ratio minimum of 4.5 percent, our G-SIB surcharge of 3.0 percent at December 31, 2024 and 2.5 percent at December 31, 2023, and SCB (under the Standardized approach) of 3.2 percent at December 31, 2024 and 2.5 percent at December 31, 2023.
The countercyclical capital buffer was zero for both periods.

The capital requirements calculated under the Capital Framework include the capital conservation buffer requirements, which are comprised of a 2.5% buffer (under the Advanced Capital Rules), the SCB (under the Standardized Capital Rules), a countercyclical capital buffer (under both Capital Rules) and the G-SIB surcharge (under both Capital Rules).
Our G-SIB surcharge is 3.0% for both 2024 and 2025 and is expected to be 3.5% beginning in 2026.

comparisons.peer_topic: Basel III CET1 and Capital Conservation Buffer Requirements
comparisons.peer_summary: Banking institutions must maintain a minimum CET1 capital ratio of 4.5% of risk-weighted assets, with certain organizations like the Firm holding additional capital conservation buffers that include a GSIB surcharge, discretionary countercyclical buffer, and a fixed 2.5% component.
comparisons.comparison: Both BAC and JPM outline the baseline CET1 capital requirements and the components of the capital conservation buffer. Both cite the 4.5% minimum CET1 ratio and the inclusion of a GSIB surcharge and a 2.5% fixed buffer component (JPM calls it capital conservation buffer for Advanced approaches, while BAC uses SCB for Standardized). JPM explicitly mentions the variable SCB and discretionary countercyclical buffer, mirroring the components disclosed by BAC.

sentences.text: (2)The CET1 capital regulatory minimum is the sum of the CET1 capital ratio minimum of 4.5 percent, our G-SIB surcharge of 3.0 percent at December 31, 2024 and 2.5 percent at December 31, 2023, and SCB (under the Standardized approach) of 3.2 percent at December 31, 2024 and 2.5 percent at December 31, 2023.
The countercyclical capital buffer was zero for both periods.
All banking institutions are currently required to have a minimum CET1 capital ratio of 4.5% of risk-weighted assets.

The capital conservation buffer incorporates a GSIB surcharge, a discretionary countercyclical capital buffer and a fixed capital conservation buffer of 2.5% for Advanced regulatory capital requirements, as well as a variable SCB requirement, floored at 2.5%, for Standardized regulatory capital requirements.

comparisons.peer_topic: Composition of CET1 Capital Buffer Requirement
comparisons.peer_summary: The CET1 capital buffer requirement represents the additional capital needed to avoid restrictions on distributions and discretionary bonuses. Under the Standardized Approach, it is the sum of the Stress Capital Buffer (SCB), G-SIB surcharge, and Countercyclical Capital Buffer (CCyB); under the Advanced Approach, it is the sum of the 2.5% capital conservation buffer, G-SIB surcharge, and CCyB.
comparisons.comparison: Both BAC and MS detail the composition of the CET1 capital buffer requirement required to avoid distribution restrictions. BAC lists the components as the SCB (3.2%) and G-SIB surcharge (3.0%) with a zero countercyclical buffer. Similarly, MS defines its buffer under the Standardized Approach as the sum of the SCB, G-SIB capital surcharge, and Countercyclical Capital Buffer (CCyB), illustrating the same regulatory framework components.

sentences.text: (2)The CET1 capital regulatory minimum is the sum of the CET1 capital ratio minimum of 4.5 percent, our G-SIB surcharge of 3.0 percent at December 31, 2024 and 2.5 percent at December 31, 2023, and SCB (under the Standardized approach) of 3.2 percent at December 31, 2024 and 2.5 percent at December 31, 2023.
The SLR regulatory minimum includes a leverage buffer of 2.0 percent.

Our capital buffer requirement computed under the standardized approaches for calculating credit risk and market RWAs ("Standardized Approach") is equal to the sum of our SCB, G-SIB capital surcharge and CCyB, and our capital buffer requirement computed under the applicable advanced approaches for calculating credit risk, market risk and operational risk RWAs ("Advanced Approach") is equal to our 2.5% capital conservation buffer, G-SIB capital surcharge and CCyB.
